content: Further exploration delves into the adoption of diverse processing technologies, such as Dense Media Separation (DMS) and jig methods, underscoring their prevalence and evolution within the industry. An analysis of commodity focus and throughput capacities across competitors offers insights into operational priorities and capacity utilization, facilitating an understanding of sector-wide benchmarks and emerging patterns. The report also investigates market signals driving demand for toll processing services. It identifies critical factors such as mining companies nearing plant capacity limits, which increasingly necessitate outsourced processing solutions. Additionally, the emergence of new mining developments lacking on-site processing facilities is linked to heightened reliance on toll services, underscoring an evolving dependency within the market. The role of washery closures and maintenance shutdowns is examined, with attention to their influence on toll processing demand cycles and coal market dynamics. Collectively, these insights provide a nuanced perspective on external pressures shaping demand trajectories. Logistical considerations form another focal point, particularly in coal transport infrastructure. While this data highlights a robust potential expansion in technological adoption across the sector, it primarily underscores future operational shifts rather than shedding light on the relevant market conditions, corporate policies, or competitive evolutions that occurred from 2020 to 2024 [3] . Further exploration of global electronic toll collection trends reveals forecasts extending well into the 2030s, yet these broader analyses consistently fail to provide regionally specific or temporally relevant data exclusively pertaining to South Africa during the historical period in question [4][5] . These sources collectively emphasize the growing role of electronic toll systems in ensuring operational efficiency and streamlining transport-related payments; however, their heavy focus on future growth trajectories undermines their direct applicability to queries requiring retrospective market analysis. Additionally, documentation stemming from South African government meetings held in May and June 2026 highlights ongoing policy discussions that could potentially affect regional infrastructure [1] .
